# Periods

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.ts from src/periods.ts. Edit those, then run `bun run docs`. -->

Every period Zhami knows, with example formats and the tokens it understands. Moment's tokens, like `YYYY` and `MMMM`, work for every period; the tables list the ones that matter most. [Name formats](formats.md) explains how they combine.

## Calendar

### Week

An ISO week, Monday to Sunday. Command: **Open this week**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GGGG-[W]WW` (default) | `2026-W46` | `2027-W01` |
| `GGGG [week] W` | `2026 week 46` | `2027 week 1` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}–{{end:D}}` | `Nov 9–15` | `Jan 4–10` |
| `GGGG/[W]WW` | `2026/W46` | `2027/W01` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `W` | Its number in the ISO year: 46 | `46` |
| `WW` | The same, with a zero: 05 | `46` |
| `Wo` | As an ordinal: 46th | `46th` |
| `GGGG` | The ISO year it belongs to. Use it with weeks, not YYYY | `2026` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 9` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 15` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

### Fortnight

Two ISO weeks: 1 and 2, 3 and 4, and so on. Command: **Open this fortnight**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GGGG-[F]{{PP}}` (default) | `2026-F23` | `2027-F01` |
| `GGGG [fortnight] {{P}}` | `2026 fortnight 23` | `2027 fortnight 1` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}–{{end:MMM D}}` | `Nov 2–Nov 15` | `Jan 4–Jan 17` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GGGG` | The ISO year it belongs to | `2026` |
| `{{P}}` | Its number in the ISO year, 1 to 27. In a year with 53 weeks, the 27th is one week long | `23` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `23rd` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `23` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 2` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 15` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

### Month

A calendar month. Command: **Open this month**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |

| `MMMM YYYY` | `November 2026` | `January 2027` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `M` | Its number: 11 | `11` |
| `MM` | With a zero: 05 | `11` |
| `MMM` | Short name: Nov | `Nov` |
| `MMMM` | Name: November | `November` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 1` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 30` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

| `Qo` | As an ordinal: 4th | `4th` |

## Seasons

### Meteorological season

Three whole months: winter is December to February in the north. Command: **Open this meteorological season**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years}}` (default) | `Autumn 2026` | `Winter 2026-27` |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years:YY-YY}}` | `Autumn 26` | `Winter 26-27` |
| `{{PPPP:fall}} {{years:YYYY-YYYY}}` | `Fall 2026` | `Winter 2026-2027` |
| `{{PPP}} YY` | `Aut 26` | `Win 26` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 4, from the season that starts in March | `3` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `3rd` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `03` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter | `Autumn` |
| `{{PPPP:fall}}` | The same, with Fall for autumn | `Fall` |
| `{{PPP}}` | Short: Spr, Sum, Aut, Win | `Aut` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Sep 1` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 30` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

### Astronomical season

From an equinox or solstice to the next. Dated in your time zone. Command: **Open this astronomical season**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years}}` (default) | `Autumn 2026` | `Winter 2026-27` |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years:YY-YY}}` | `Autumn 26` | `Winter 26-27` |
| `{{PPPP:fall}} {{years:YYYY-YYYY}}` | `Fall 2026` | `Winter 2026-2027` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 4, from the March equinox | `3` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `3rd` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `03` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter | `Autumn` |
| `{{PPPP:fall}}` | The same, with Fall for autumn | `Fall` |
| `{{PPP}}` | Short: Spr, Sum, Aut, Win | `Aut` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Sep 23` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Dec 20` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

Equinoxes and solstices come from the sun's position, computed with VSOP87 and the methods in Jean Meeus, *Astronomical Algorithms*.

### Wheel of the Year

Eight festivals: the solstices, the equinoxes, and the days between. Dated in your time zone, for the solstices and equinoxes. Command: **Open this festival of the Wheel of the Year**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years}}` (default) | `Samhain 2026` | `Yule 2026-27` |
| `YYYY {{PPPP}}` | `2026 Samhain` | `2026 Yule` |
| `{{PP}} {{PPPP}} YYYY` | `01 Samhain 2026` | `02 Yule 2026` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 8, from Samhain | `1` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `1st` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `01` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | The festival: Samhain, Yule, Imbolc, Ostara, Beltane, Litha, Lughnasadh, Mabon | `Samhain` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 1` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Dec 20` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

Imbolc, Beltane, Lughnasadh and Samhain fall on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, their traditional dates. Ostara, Litha, Mabon and Yule are the equinoxes and solstices. In the southern hemisphere, the festivals move by half a year: Yule is at the June solstice.

## Work

### Fashion season

Spring-summer and fall-winter, from dates you choose. Command: **Open this fashion season**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPP}}YY` (default) | `FW26` | `FW26` |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years}}` | `Fall-winter 2026-27` | `Fall-winter 2026-27` |
| `{{PPP:autumn}}YY` | `AW26` | `AW26` |
| `YYYY {{PPP}}` | `2026 FW` | `2026 FW` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 for spring-summer, 2 for fall-winter | `2` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `2nd` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `02` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name: Spring-summer, Fall-winter | `Fall-winter` |
| `{{PPPP:autumn}}` | The same, with Autumn-winter | `Autumn-winter` |
| `{{PPP}}` | Short: SS, FW | `FW` |
| `{{PPP:autumn}}` | Short, with AW: SS, AW | `AW` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Aug 1` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Jan 31` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026-27` |

Settings: **Spring-summer starts**, default `02-01`; **Fall-winter starts**, default `08-01`.

The defaults follow the retail calendar of the National Retail Federation, where spring-summer runs from February to July and fall-winter from August to January. Brands differ, so both start dates are settings.

## Japan

### Sekki

The 24 sekki (二十四節気), about 15 days each, from Risshun in early February. Dated in Japan time. Command: **Open this sekki**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} YYYY` (default) | `Rittō 2026` | `Shōkan 2027` |
| `YYYY {{PPPP:kanji}}` | `2026 立冬` | `2027 小寒` |
| `{{PPPP:english}} YYYY` | `Beginning of winter 2026` | `Lesser cold 2027` |
| `YYYY-{{PP}} {{PPPP}}` | `2026-19 Rittō` | `2027-23 Shōkan` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 24, from Risshun | `19` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `19th` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `19` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name in romaji: Rittō | `Rittō` |
| `{{PPPP:kanji}}` | In kanji: 立冬 | `立冬` |
| `{{PPPP:english}}` | In English: Beginning of winter | `Beginning of winter` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 7` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 21` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

Romaji and English from Nippon.com, [Japan's 72 Microseasons](https://www.nippon.com/en/features/h00124/). A sekki starts when the sun reaches its longitude, every 15° from 315°, dated in Japan time, as the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan does.

### Kō

The 72 kō (七十二候), about 5 days each, three in every sekki. Dated in Japan time. Command: **Open this kō**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP:english}} YYYY` (default) | `Land starts to freeze 2026` | `Springs thaw 2027` |
| `YYYY-{{PP}} {{PPPP:kanji}}` | `2026-56 地始凍` | `2027-68 水泉動` |
| `{{PPPP}} YYYY` | `Chi hajimete kōru 2026` | `Shimizu atataka o fukumu 2027` |
| `{{PPPP:sekki}} {{P}}` | `Rittō 56` | `Shōkan 68` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 72, from the first kō of Risshun | `56` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `56th` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `56` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name in romaji: Tsubaki hajimete hiraku | `Chi hajimete kōru` |
| `{{PPPP:kanji}}` | In kanji: 山茶始開 | `地始凍` |
| `{{PPPP:kana}}` | In kana: つばきはじめてひらく | `ちはじめてこおる` |
| `{{PPPP:english}}` | In English: Camellias bloom | `Land starts to freeze` |
| `{{PPPP:sekki}}` | The sekki it's in, in romaji: Rittō | `Rittō` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 12` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 16` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

The 72 kō of the 1874 *Ryakuhonreki* (略本暦). Kanji and kana from Japanese Wikipedia, [七十二候](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/七十二候); romaji and English from [Nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/features/h00124/). Readings of the kō aren't standardized, so other sources may read them differently. Each kō is 5° of the sun's longitude.

| `{{PPPP:hanzi}}` | The animal in characters: 马 | `马` |
| `{{PPPP:ganzhi}}` | The year's stem and branch: 丙午 | `丙午` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Feb 17` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Feb 5` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026-27` |

Lunar New Year from the Hong Kong Observatory's [Gregorian-Lunar calendar conversion tables](https://www.hko.gov.hk/en/gts/time/conversion.htm), 1901 to 2100. The element and stem-branch follow the sexagenary cycle.

## Korea

### Jeolgi

The 24 jeolgi (절기), about 15 days each, from Ipchun in early February. Dated in Korea time (UTC+9). Command: **Open this jeolgi**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} YYYY` (default) | `Ipdong 2026` | `Sohan 2027` |
| `YYYY {{PPPP:hangul}}` | `2026 입동` | `2027 소한` |
| `{{PPPP:english}} YYYY` | `Beginning of winter 2026` | `Minor cold 2027` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 24, from Ipchun | `19` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `19th` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `19` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name, romanized: Ipdong | `Ipdong` |
| `{{PPPP:hangul}}` | In Hangul: 입동 | `입동` |
| `{{PPPP:english}}` | In English: Beginning of winter | `Beginning of winter` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Nov 7` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Nov 21` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

Names from English Wikipedia, [Solar term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_term), in South Korean spelling. Dated in Korea time.

## India

### Ṛtu

Six seasons of about two months, from Vasanta in mid-February. Śiśira starts at the winter solstice. Dated in India time (UTC+5:30). Command: **Open this ṛtu**.

| Format | Nov 13, 2026 | Jan 10, 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{PPPP}} {{years}}` (default) | `Hemanta 2026` | `Śiśira 2026-27` |
| `YYYY {{PPPP:devanagari}}` | `2026 हेमन्त` | `2026 शिशिर` |
| `{{PPPP:english}} {{years}}` | `Pre-winter 2026` | `Winter 2026-27` |

| Token | Gives | Nov 13, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{P}}` | 1 to 6, from Vasanta | `5` |
| `{{Po}}` | The same, as an ordinal: 1st, 2nd, 3rd | `5th` |
| `{{PP}}` | The same, with a zero: 01, 02 | `05` |
| `{{PPPP}}` | Its name: Vasanta, Grīṣma, Varṣā, Śarad, Hemanta, Śiśira | `Hemanta` |
| `{{PPPP:plain}}` | Without diacritics: Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemanta, Shishira | `Hemanta` |
| `{{PPPP:devanagari}}` | In Devanagari: हेमन्त | `हेमन्त` |
| `{{PPPP:english}}` | In English: Pre-winter | `Pre-winter` |
| `{{start:MMM D}}` | The first day, in any moment format. Default: YYYY-MM-DD | `Oct 23` |
| `{{end:MMM D}}` | The last day, the same way | `Dec 21` |
| `{{years:YYYY-YY}}` | Its year, or both years when it crosses New Year. Default: YYYY-YY | `2026` |

Ṛtu here follow the tropical sun, as [Drik Panchang](https://www.drikpanchang.com/seasons/season-tropical-timings.html) dates them: Śiśira starts at the winter solstice, and each ṛtu spans 60° of the sun's longitude. Calendars that count ṛtu by lunar months, like Chaitra and Vaishakha for Vasanta, run up to a month later.
